sources.note: Brief uses mm and N*m; use mm and N, with 40 N*m = 40000 N*mm.
Envelope 160 mm in x and 80 mm in y and z; y up, origin at minimum corner.
Steel is stated; assume isotropic linear-elastic steel E=210000 N/mm^2 and nu=0.3 because grade and elastic constants are unspecified.
Brief specifies volume fraction 0.3; applied to design volume excluding passive lugs per tool convention.
Brief specifies 2 mm elements; h=2 mm.
Brief says x=0 end bolted rigidly to gearbox; clamp entire end face in x, y and z.
16x16 top lug flush y=80 has centroid (x,y,z)=(160,72,40). Bottom centroid y=8, separation 64 mm. F=40000/64=625 N. Top +z and bottom -z give positive right-hand-rule x torque.
16x16 bottom lug flush y=0 has centroid (160,8,40). Equal opposite force -625 N along z; net force zero and Mx=625*(72-8)=40000 N*mm.
Preserve stated top 16x16 end-face lug as solid over y=64..80 and z=32..48; assume 4 mm axial depth x=156..160 inside envelope.
Preserve stated bottom 16x16 end-face lug as solid over y=0..16 and z=32..48; assume 4 mm axial depth x=156..160 inside envelope.

final: DONE, assumptions: isotropic steel with E = 210 GPa and ν = 0.3; solid drive lugs extend 4 mm inward. Validation passed, render confirmed placement, and every item is source-tagged.

spec.description: 160 x 80 x 80 mm shaft bracket, y up. Clamp x=0. Apply +40 N*m about x through equal opposite z forces on 16 x 16 mm end-face drive lugs. Assume 4 mm axial solid lug depth within envelope and isotropic linear-elastic steel E=210 GPa, nu=0.3.
